result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.clear_selection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Clear all node and edge selections. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20625-L20698){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.clear_selection() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Clear selection](/assets/graphs/clear-selection.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: nodes B and E and the edge between them are selected in the accent color. After clear_selection, nothing is selected: every node and edge is plain." width="100%"} Empties both the node selection and the edge selection in one step. The nodes and edges themselves, and their attributes, are untouched; only the selection state is reset. All `select_*` methods add to the existing selection rather than replacing it, so calling `clear_selection()` before building a new selection is the usual way to make sure nothing left over from an earlier step leaks into the next `*_ws` operation. It is also safe to call when nothing is selected. To remove only some nodes or edges from the selection, use `deselect_nodes()` or `deselect_edges()`. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub of this star is selected by degree and then the selection is cleared, so no nodes remain selected: ::: {#345af038 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(5) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=3) .clear_selection() ) graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: Without clearing, selections accumulate. Here the second selection rule adds to the first (the hub plus the last two spokes), while clearing between the two calls leaves only the result of the second: ::: {#00c2e6f6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5) graph.select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=3).select_last_nodes_created(2) accumulated = graph.count_selected_nodes() graph.clear_selection().select_last_nodes_created(2) fresh = graph.count_selected_nodes() (accumulated, fresh) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 2) ``` ::: ::: Node and edge selections are reset together. Here the two nodes from the last step are still selected and all four spoke edges are added; one call clears both: ::: {#766eaf68 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} hub = graph.get_node_creation_order()[0] graph.select_edges_by_node([hub]).clear_selection() (graph.count_selected_nodes(), graph.count_selected_edges()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (0, 0) ``` ::: :::
